data.content_ref: inline:The target's mechanism commits a definitional conflation that makes its 'dissolution' trivially vacuous. By defining corroboration as 'merely the label for not yet eliminated,' the target erases the distinction between (a) a theory that has survived severe critical testing and (b) a theory that has never been tested at all. Both are 'not yet eliminated' under the target's framework, so both would be acted on identically by the 'Eliminative Default.' But the entire non-trivial content of the corroboration concept—Popper's point—is that a theory surviving severe tests has been critically scrutinized in ways an untested theory has not, yielding a structural difference in epistemic status. The target's relabeling does not dissolve the dilemma; it merely renames 'corroboration' to 'non-elimination' and then declares the problem solved, while silently destroying the very distinction that made the problem meaningful. The claim that 'the underlying structure was never relevant to the outcome at all' is not a discovery but an artifact of this equivocation: if you define away the distinction between well-tested and untested survivors, of course the structure becomes irrelevant—but that is the distinction the original question was asking about.
